newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England signals no change in rates.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England signals no change in rates.

text.p: The Bank of England signalled that it had left official interest rates unchanged at 6.0 percent after Wednesday's monetary policy meeting by offering the money market routine assistance.
The Bank normally announces any change in interest rates by setting a new minimum lending rate during its money market operations. The absence of any announcement showed rates were unchanged.

There was still a possibility that the central bank could announce a rate change on Thursday morning, but a Reuters poll of economists before Wednesday's meeting showed 23 out of 24 expected no change in policy.

British monetary policy is set by Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke, who takes advice from Bank of England Governor Eddie George at monthly meetings. The two men have been at odds over policy in recent months. George, who fears inflation pressures are building up, has been urging Clarke to raise official interest rates.

The Chancellor, anxious to avoid raising rates in the run-up to the looming election as this would mean dearer home loans for millions of Britons, has so far refused, arguing that the economic signals are mixed.
